questions.question: Giant anteaters are totally silent, but their offspring would whistle shrilly when they feel threatened.
questions.explanation: Esta frase incluye los verbos «are» y «feel», en presente, junto con el verbo «would whistle», en condicional. El presente no debe utilizarse con «would». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «would» por «will».

questions.question: After he served as an envoy to China in 1974, George Bush has become president of the United States.

questions.question: Beethoven began to lose his hearing in 1798 and has become completely deaf by 1824.
questions.explanation: Esta frase incluye el verbo «has become» en presente perfecto y la expresión temporal del pluscuamperfecto «by 1824». El presente perfecto no debe utilizarse con esta expresión temporal. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «has become» por «had become».

questions.question: If a person were to look up from the bottom of a deep well, he will be able to see stars in the middle of the day.

questions.question: Relatively small overdoses of acetaminophen have recently blamed by American doctors for liver damage and even deaths in children.

questions.question: Lithium batteries are extremely reliable, so they used to power military radios, pacemakers, watches, and memory backups for computers.

questions.question: Koalas drink so few water that zookeepers become concerned if a koala wants to drink any water.
questions.explanation: Esta frase incluye el cuantificador contable «few» junto con el sustantivo incontable «water». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «few» por «little».

questions.question: Arctic animals' feet is covered with hair on their soles to help them walk on ice and snow.

questions.question: Without formal training as a geographer, cartographer, or engraving, James Wilson began producing the first American-made globes in 1810.

questions.question: Because fat is needed for mylenization, fat should not be restricted in the diet of a normal weight children under the age of two.

questions.question: Hummingbirds inhabit much of the world's most extreme climates.

questions.question: The residence of Greenville, Texas hold an annual Cotton Jubilee to remember the crop that caused their city to prosper.

questions.question: Although the climate is frigid, polar bears, musk oxes, caribous, Arctic foxes, and penguins inhabit the polar regions.

questions.question: In winter, various animals go into hibernation during which theirs breathing is reduced to a minimum.

questions.question: Some ancient philosophers such as Pythagorus and Aristotle were ahead of their time because he thought that the Earth was round.

questions.question: If you touch something cold, the molecules in yours fingers slow down and lose heat.

questions.question: Writer Mark Twain was born in 1835, the year of Halley's comet, and his died in 1910, the year that Halley's comet returned.

questions.question: The praying mantis devours poisonous insects as well as their own kind.
questions.explanation: El adjetivo posesivo plural «their» se refiere al sustantivo singular «mantis religiosa». Un adjetivo posesivo debe concordar con el sustantivo al que se refiere. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «their» por «its».

questions.question: Anyone who lives along the San Andreas fault should be sure that they are prepared for an earthquake.

questions.question: A drupe is a kind of soft fruit that has a hardstone simple, just like plums and ordinary cherries.

questions.question: A harmless shark called the Rhincodan typus is the largest of its kind and general eats only plankton, small fish, and squid.

questions.question: In 80 A.D. the Colosseum in Rome became the first stadium domed to be opened to the public.

questions.question: The oboe, which is considered the most difficult instrument to play proficiently, does produce, however, bright colors and a richly tone.

questions.question: According to Dr. Kenneth Cooper, an average person needs to exercise three times per week for 45 minutes each time in order to look and feel healthily.

questions.question: Everglades National Park in Florida is virtually a wilderness subtropical filled with abundant plant and animal life.

questions.question: The Aztecs, an ancient civilization in Central America, were the first to make deliciously chocolate from the cocoa pod.

questions.question: The pantelgraph, which was invented in 1856 in France, proved quite successfully as the forerunner of the modern-day fax machine.

questions.question: The swirling winds of a tornado can reach quickly speeds close to 300 miles per hour.

questions.question: The extermination of a single species in any food chain can affect drastically all others.

questions.question: The Indian leaf butterfly looks like an old leaf on a branch when it disguises naturally itself.

questions.question: The most frequently sung song in the world, "Happy Birthday To You," was actually written with other set of words by the Hill sisters in 1893.
